threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 38 bus will take you anywhere on time. Locals know better than to trust the clock around here.
Last night on the 35, a guy sang every word of ‘Wonderwall’ like he was in the Royal Albert Hall. A proper audience joined in halfway.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in full dirndl confidently ordering a kebab at 2 AM. Only in Neukölln do cultures blend like that.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you’ll find random techno raves in the U-Bahn tunnels. Just a regular Saturday night, complete with neon lights and an underground vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows that the smells wafting from the taquerias change with the weather, spicy one day, sweet the next.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy at the Civic Center Muni stop with a cat on a leash. Turns out it was the cat that was leading him—total role reversal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Many tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals use them for real conversations and late-night gatherings. They miss the vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their tendency to walk into the wrong bar, ordering a 'café con leche' in the evening like it’s normal.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of the 'Underground'—loud and clear you’re new to the East.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken from a late-night stall while waiting for the bus. It's always the same guy, flipping patties like it's a secret art.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the scent of Turkish bread wafted through the streets, mixing with the hum of late-night kebab shops and laughter.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a club that doubles as a church on weekends, complete with a techno mass. It's surreal and oddly spiritual.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know not to panic during a BART delay – just grab a burrito and settle in for the wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that stopped for a street performer mid-ride. The whole bus clapped when the song ended. Pure SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the parks and plazas, but it’s the hidden boutiques and local bakeries that truly pulse with life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they order 'café con leche' at any hour—only tourists sip it after 11 AM.
